title: The Kidneys That Kept Growing
synopsis: A 28-year-old man with blood in his urine, bilateral flank pain, and a family history of polycystic kidney disease arrives hypertensive and in distress. His enlarged kidneys are palpable, his blood pressure is 162/98, and the clock is ticking on a hidden berry aneurysm.

chapters.heading: Arrival
chapters.body: Mr. Sheng Liang, 28, walks into the ED clutching his lower back, his face pale and tight. His blood pressure is 162/98, pulse 98, SpO2 95% — he is hypertensive, tachycardic, and in visible discomfort. He tells the triage nurse he has been passing blood for two days and the flank pain is now constant, bilateral, and deep.
chapters.visualHint: Third-person oversight from the ED bay door — Mr. Liang sits on the gurney in a blue gown, both hands pressed against his lower back, bare feet dangling over the mattress edge. Monitor shows BP 162/98, HR 98. A urine sample bag sits on the bedside table.

chapters.heading: Embodiment
chapters.body: On exam, the attending palpates his abdomen and feels two firm, knobby masses in both flanks — each the size of a grapefruit, tender to touch. The patient winces and says, 'It feels like someone is squeezing my kidneys from inside.' The hematuria is visible in the sample: dark, cola-colored urine.
chapters.visualHint: Close-up on the attending's hands pressing into the right flank — the patient's face contorts in pain. Behind him, the urine sample bag is dark red-brown. The monitor beeps steadily.

chapters.heading: Escalation
chapters.body: A bedside renal ultrasound reveals massive bilateral kidneys studded with dozens of anechoic cysts — some simple, some complex with internal echoes from recent hemorrhage. The largest cyst on the right measures 6 cm and shows layering debris, confirming acute bleeding into a cyst. The left kidney is similarly enlarged, with cysts compressing the renal pelvis. The attending notes the declining renal function on the BMP: creatinine 1.8 mg/dL, eGFR 42.
chapters.visualHint: Ultrasound screen in the ED bay — a transverse view of the right kidney shows multiple black circles (cysts) of varying sizes, one with a fluid-debris level. The attending points to the screen while the patient watches from the gurney.

chapters.heading: Crisis Point
chapters.body: The blood pressure remains stubbornly high at 160/96 despite the patient's discomfort. The attending orders a CTA of the head to screen for a berry aneurysm — a known complication of ADPKD that can rupture without warning. The patient's father had polycystic kidney disease, and the genetic risk to his own future children is 50%. The team starts lisinopril 5 mg to control the hypertension and protect the remaining nephrons.
chapters.visualHint: The patient lies back on the gurney, eyes closed, as a nurse places an IV in his right arm. The monitor shows BP 160/96. A radiology tech wheels in a portable CT scanner. The attending reviews the consent form for the head CTA.

chapters.heading: Recontextualization
chapters.body: The head CTA returns negative for aneurysm — a relief, but not a cure. Mr. Liang is admitted for blood pressure control, pain management, and nephrology consultation. He will need lifelong monitoring of kidney function, blood pressure, and annual head imaging for aneurysm screening. Genetic counseling is arranged for him and his family. The flank pain slowly improves with hydration and analgesia, but the underlying disease — a genetic time bomb in every cell — remains.
chapters.visualHint: Mr. Liang sits up in the hospital bed, now in a standard gown, a blanket over his legs. A nephrologist sits beside him, holding a tablet showing a diagram of the kidneys. The patient's face is tired but calm. The window shows evening light.
